answer: A numbered mirror rests in a velvet case at a lookout; its flash across the ocean is the proof. At noon the holder takes the mirror once and flashes sun to the station, and the keeper logs the flash on a dated card. Two verifiers at the station match flash and number within 24 hours; a mirror never flashed, or a duplicate number, locks the account and burns its deposit. One flash is cheap; 100 fakes need 100 mirrors and 100 trips.
